definitions: to officially make a claim, request, or offer
to spend time doing something, especially working
to insert something into something else
to contribute something, such as effort or money
to interrupt a conversation to say something
examples: She put in a claim for damages.
He put in a lot of hours on that project.
Don't forget to put in the plug.
They all put in some money for the gift.
He kept putting in his opinion.
pastTenses: put in (past simple), put in (present perfect)
